newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean prosecutors give strike leaders ultimatum.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean prosecutors give strike leaders ultimatum.

text.p: South Korean state prosecutors on Wednesday issued an ultimatum to strike leaders to drop industrial action immediately or face arrest.

"If the current illegal action is not halted right away we will exercise our prosecution power sternly and resolutely to maintain national order," prosecutor Choi Byung-kook told a news conference. The prosecution has arrest warrants on seven strike leaders sheltering in a Seoul cathedral.
Choi also raised the threat of enemy North Korea using industrial unrest to attack the government of President Kim Young-sam.
"North Korea is agitating workers to topple the government," he said. "If the unrest drags on it will give North Korea an opportunity for revolutionary struggle."

Illegal strikes were damaging the economy and escalating a sense of national crisis. "If labour unrest continues, it will deal a serious blow to the nation's economy and the people's daily lives," he said.
Choi also warned the nation's educated elite against taking sides with strikers.
